title: Upgrade comms matrix and channelized changelogs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a channel-specific upgrade communications matrix and a set of channelized changelog templates to support LTS and non-LTS rollouts. This ticket consolidates messaging for canary / staged releases, Dedicated/Private upgrade guidance, and automation hooks for the upgrade tooling to emit per-customer, per-channel notices. The goal is predictable customer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while minimizing support load during version transitions.
acceptance_criteria: A single comms matrix mapping customer segment, trigger (canary/GA/forced), and recommended delivery channel exists
Changelog templates for email, in-console banner, API release notes, and engineering changelogs are written and approved
Automation spec for upgrade-tooling to emit personalized notices (using metadata: customer tier, LTS subscription, region) is documented
Two sample migration guides (Hosted -> minor upgrade, Dedicated -> LTS major upgrade) published to Drive and linked from the console
Stakeholder signoff from Support, Security, and Sales on customer impact and recommended cadence
deliverables: Comms matrix CSV and annotated PDF (channels: email, console, in-product banner, dashboard card, direct account outreach)
Four channel-specific changelog templates (Email, Console Summary, API Release Notes, Markdown migration guide)
Sample subject lines and short-copy variants for high/low urgency scenarios
Automation hook spec (webhook + templating variables) for release-engineering to integrate with upgrade tooling
Two example migration guides and a rollback checklist
tasks: Draft comms matrix and map to existing subscription segments (self-serve, Dedicated, Private/VPC)
Draft and review channel-specific changelog templates with Support and Legal
Coordinate with Release Engineering on webhook payloads and template variables
Publish sample migration guides to Drive and link into Console release notes section
Run tabletop exercise with Support to validate messaging and escalation paths
example_messages:
Email (canary notice) - Subject: Early access: runtime-1.18 canary rollout for your account
Body: Hi <CustomerName>, we are starting a limited canary of runtime-1.18 that includes performance batching and a KV cache tweak. No action required for this canary. Expected window: 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-17. Contact support@redwood.ai for questions.

Email (GA notice) - Subject: Action recommended: upcoming runtime-1.18 LTS upgrade
Body: Hello <CustomerName>, runtime-1.18 (LTS) will be available on 2025-04-01. If you are on Dedicated or Private, please schedule your upgrade by 2025-04-15 via the console. See migration guide: <drive-link>. Known breaking changes: authentication header deprecation (see migration steps).
Console banner (short) - runtime-1.18 LTS available · Review changes & schedule upgrade

Console release note (long) - runtime-1.18 includes: 1) batching algorithm improvements (15% median cost reduction), 2) kernel selection fixes to reduce tail latency, 3) API header deprecation for legacy auth. Impact: self-serve hosted customers will be auto-rolled unless opted out; Dedicated/Private require scheduling. Action: review migration guide and run workloads in canary environment.
In-product card (supported) - Title: Upgrade window for runtime-1.18 · Open schedule · Impact: possible brief cold-starts during migration
migration_guide_outline: Overview: What changes in runtime-1.18 and why it matters
Compatibility: list of deprecated headers and config flags
Pre-upgrade checklist: test prompts, snapshot KV, review load profile
Canary run: steps to join canary, validate tokenized metrics, and compare outputs
Upgrade steps: scheduling, expected downtime (if any), roll-forward commands
Rollback steps: immediate mitigation steps, restore from snapshot, open support ticket
Post-upgrade checks: latency/cost dashboards, regression tests, feedback collection
rollback_steps: If model outputs degrade: immediately enable fallback routing to previous model variant via Console > Rollouts
If latency regressions exceed SLO: trigger autoscaling override and engage on-call infra
If config incompatibility: apply saved pre-upgrade config and restart nodes; follow dedicated rollback playbook
Open incident with Release Engineering and tag with release id runtime-1.18 and customer id

2025-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Pulled in Support for review; suggested adding a low-friction 'opt-out' path for self-serve hosted customers during canary.
2025-02-27 - Chris Nguyen (Support): Reviewed templates, requested clearer escalation CTA and a dedicated support alias for LTS migrations.
2025-03-01 - Priya Shah (Security): Confirmed no PII in templated emails; recommended removing raw debug links from public changelogs.
2025-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Engineering to confirm whether upgrade-tooling can populate customer region in webhook payloads (pending GH PR).
2025-03-05 - Release Eng: PR #1294 adds templating variables and sample payload; requesting review for webhook schema. Next: update migration guide with exact command snippets.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: frequency of emails vs. support load — we recommend fewer, higher-value messages (canary + GA + critical hotfix) and rely on console for status updates.
Trade-off: personalized notices increase fidelity but require integration work into upgrade tooling; we provide a baseline template to ship early and incremental personalization later.
Decision: For Dedicated customers we'll require a scheduled upgrade window; for Hosted customers we'll offer an opt-out during the first canary wave.
